error_cases.subject: alibaba
error_cases.pattern_hypothesis: Adjacent top-to-main progression flagged as jump
error_cases.observable_characteristics: The transition goes from the header language selector to the next focusable element in the page's main area, described as the main content / sign-in panel link. In navigation_order, these are consecutive meaningful positions 2 -> 3 and implemented labels 5 -> 6. The screenshots show the selector near the logo at top left and the next focus target as a large main-content region/link below, which is a plausible section-to-section progression rather than an obviously disordered jump.
error_cases.matching_criteria: A transition where source and destination are consecutive in the inferred meaningful order, move from a header control into the main content area, and do not visibly skip intermediate focusable controls within that area.
error_cases.possible_cause: The detector may have over-weighted spatial distance or region change between header and main content, treating a normal cross-section move as a linear-navigation failure despite consecutive semantic order.
error_cases.supporting_evidence: evaluated_transitions marks this exact transition FP; navigation_order lists language selector at position 2 and main content / sign-in panel link at position 3; kfg contains the TAB edge /html[1]/body[1]/div[1]/div[2]/select[1] -> /html[1]/body[1]/div[2]/div[2]/div[1]/a[1]; screenshots show no visible intermediate top-level control between them.

error_cases.subject: alibaba
error_cases.pattern_hypothesis: Inline recovery link hides skipped primary control
error_cases.observable_characteristics: Within the sign-in form, focus goes from the "Forgot Password?" link to the "Stay signed in" checkbox. The inferred meaningful order places these at positions 7 -> 8, but the screenshots show the password input and forgot-password link sharing the password row, with the checkbox below them. The implemented order therefore bypasses the primary password-field sequence and places an auxiliary link before the checkbox. Ground truth labels this transition as an LNF.
error_cases.matching_criteria: A transition inside a form where an auxiliary inline link associated with a field is focused before lower form controls, and the subsequent move continues downward while a nearby primary field/control in the same field group has been bypassed or reordered.
error_cases.possible_cause: The detector may have relied heavily on inferred positions and direct adjacency, concluding that 7 -> 8 looked orderly, while missing that the source is an auxiliary link visually tied to the password row and that the implemented path creates a problematic within-form sequence.
error_cases.supporting_evidence: evaluated_transitions marks this exact transition FN; navigation_order identifies the source as "Forgot Password? link" and destination as "Stay signed in checkbox"; kfg contains the TAB edge from the forgot-password link to the checkbox; screenshots show the forgot-password link on the password row and the checkbox below, indicating a local form-order irregularity rather than a simple adjacent progression.

error_cases.matching_criteria: A transition should match when it is an observed forward Tab transition between adjacent implemented focus targets, but the two targets belong to visually or functionally separated regions and the earlier region already contains a focus-order irregularity that may affect interpretation of the later jump.
error_cases.possible_cause: Observed evidence shows the detector did not report this ground-truth LNF even though the transition is present in Stage 1 and KFG. A plausible but unverified cause is that the detector primarily keyed on direct inversions between implemented labels and inferred meaningful positions, which would catch the Sign in button -> Forgot password? link reversal but not this subsequent forward move from label 4 to 5. Another unverified possibility is that the detector treated adjacent forward Tab moves as normal even when the ground truth considered the surrounding sequence slightly disordered.
